name: Tool Calls Need A Last Enforceable Boundary
text: Admission evidence is not execution authority. PACE shows why a safe and a leaking artifact can present the same admission evidence, then evaluates effect verification against authority compiled from the authenticated request immediately before a tool call executes. That mechanism extends the requirement for a last enforceable boundary. It does not evaluate reputation systems, prove the categorical institutional rule, or establish performance across all sovereign-runtime coordination layers.
scope_conditions: tool-using agents acting under authenticated user requests

sourceProvenance.sourceProposition: Pre-admission artifact vetting cannot settle authority when safe and leaking variants share admission evidence; enforcing schema-defined effects against authenticated request authority immediately before tool execution supplies the last actionable boundary.
sourceProvenance.exactEvidenceQuote: Vetting an artifact before admission does not settle this. A safe variant and a leaking variant can produce the same admission evidence, and a sound gate then cannot relax that site for either. We make that condition precise, which leaves the last boundary a deployment can still act on. We present Provenance-Aware Capability Enforcement (PACE), which mediates every tool call immediately before it executes. Path confinement proposes an executable cut of represented influence paths, while capability and effect verification checks schema-defined effects against authority compiled from the authenticated request.
